speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry has plans to provide or to encourage the provision of night-time childcare beyond the three night-care centres run by the Morning Star charity, for low-income parents who have to work night shifts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The current arrangement meets the needs of most parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But for those working shifts or on weekends, many of them arrange for other caregivers, such as grandparents and relatives, to help out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That will also look into programming that meets the needs of the residents in rental housing, who are mostly low-income households.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These include certain kinds of caregiving that they may require.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we look at requirements based on locality as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, is it a confirmation that we are looking into providing more night-time childcare services in certain areas?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because I see on the ground that some of the parents who have to work the night shift, they leave their children at home, in fear of their safety, and then they go and work, especially for a lot of the single parents.
